opening_message:
Ticket 1: Jesse Stewart (employee ID E013) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E013.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: admin
  - comment: Jesse Stewart (E013) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, so admin is permitted. Recommend granting admin as requested.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Jesse Stewart (E013) is a contractor with basic security training, not full-time as noted earlier. Contractors can never have admin. With basic training, max access is read. Recommend granting read.
reason: The two notes conflict on employment type: HR's database says Jesse Stewart is full-time Payroll Specialist (which would permit admin since Payroll is owned by that role), but Security's database lookup says Jesse is a contractor with basic security training, and Security explicitly flags the earlier full-time claim as incorrect. Contractors can never be granted admin, and with basic training their maximum access is read. Because the requested level (admin) exceeds the permissible maximum under the contractor classification, and the conservative reading of the conflicting evidence must respect the "never admin" rule for contractors, I grant read.

- Security agent says: contractor, basic security training. Recommendation: read. Also claims Security DB shows contractor, not full-time.

The access policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if the employee's role owns the system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if they have advanced security training. Never admin.

Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role.

If the employee is full-time Payroll Specialist: admin is permitted (role owns system).
If the employee is contractor: never admin, max is read (basic training).
